name: scroll-progress
title: Scroll Progress
description: A reading progress bar pinned to the top of the viewport, shaded from purple through pink to peach, that fills further the more of the page you scroll.
use: A long article or docs page should show at a glance how much is left to read.
avoid: Short pages, where the strip never moves and just adds a coloured line.
a11y: The bar has no role or aria value, so screen readers are given no sense of reading position. (keyboard: n-a, labels: n-a, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A slim gradient strip of purple, pink and peach glued to the very top edge of a dark article page. The strip is only a few pixels tall and spans from the left either partway or all the way across, depending on how far the page has been scrolled.
behaves: The bar starts as a short stub at the left and stretches to the right in step with vertical scroll, reaching the full width at the bottom of the page. It stays fixed while the article moves underneath.
customise: Height and position are set through the class name; the three gradient colours are hardcoded hex values in the source.
weight: light: A single fixed element whose horizontal scale reads the scroll position; no loop.
